title: Decode throughput across three local runtimes
subtitle: Single 35B model, one machine, identical prompts
summary: We pointed llama.cpp, vLLM and MLX at the same 35B model on one host and measured time-to-first-token and sustained decode rate over a 24-turn session replay.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body:
Each runtime served the same quantized 35B checkpoint on the same host, with no other load.

We replayed a recorded 24-turn coding session against each server and recorded per-turn wall time, time-to-first-token, and reported token counts.
bullets: Identical prompts and generation caps across runtimes
Warm cache: one discarded priming run before measurement

sections.heading: What surprised us
sections.body: The spread in time-to-first-token was much wider than the spread in decode rate. Two runtimes within 4% of each other on sustained decode differed by more than 2x on TTFT, which is the number a user actually feels while typing.
